cards.front: What is the primary goal of Speaker Identification in audio biometrics?
cards.back: Determining the identity of a speaker from a known or unknown set of individuals.

cards.front: How does Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) differ from Speaker Identification?
cards.back: ASR transcribes spoken language into text, whereas Speaker Identification determines who is speaking.

cards.front: What is the primary function of Voice Anti-Spoofing in a voice biometrics pipeline?
cards.back: Detecting whether an audio sample is from a live human or synthetic speech (deepfake).

cards.front: What physical organ's vibration determines the fundamental frequency ($F_0$) of a human voice?
cards.back: The vocal folds (vocal cords) in the larynx.

cards.front: What is the typical fundamental frequency ($F_0$) range for adult male voices during phonation?
cards.back: 85 Hz to 180 Hz.

cards.front: What is the typical fundamental frequency ($F_0$) range for adult female voices during phonation?
cards.back: 165 Hz to 255 Hz.

cards.front: Anatomic correlates: Formants $F_1$ and $F_2$ primarily correspond to _____ movement during speech articulation.
cards.back: tongue

cards.front: Which formants are most informative for individual speaker identification due to vocal tract geometry?
cards.back: Formants $F_3$, $F_4$, and higher.

cards.front: Concept: Jitter in acoustic phonetics
cards.back: Definition: The cycle-to-cycle variation of fundamental frequency ($F_0$) periods.

cards.front: Concept: Shimmer in acoustic phonetics
cards.back: Definition: The cycle-to-cycle variation of vocal amplitude between adjacent speech periods.

cards.front: What does a high Harmonics-to-Noise Ratio (HNR) indicate regarding voice quality?
cards.back: A clear, resonant voice with minimal turbulent noise from incomplete vocal fold closure.

cards.front: What standard acoustic feature representation replaces MFCCs as the input to modern deep neural networks like ResNet and TDNN?
cards.back: Log-Mel Filterbanks (Fbanks).

cards.front: What frame length and frame shift are standard for computing Log-Mel Filterbanks in speaker embedding extractors?
cards.back: A 25 ms frame length with a 10 ms frame shift.

cards.front: In biometrics, Open-Set Speaker Identification differs from Closed-Set Identification by allowing the candidate to be _____.
cards.back: Out-of-Set (an unmonitored or unknown individual)

cards.front: What formula describes the Open-Set False Alarm Rate ($FAR_{OSI}$) given watchlist size $N$ and $1:1$ $FAR_{1:1}$?
cards.back: $FAR_{OSI} = 1 - (1 - FAR_{1:1})^N \approx N \cdot FAR_{1:1}$

cards.front: According to the VoxWatch benchmark, expanding watchlist size from 50 to 500 increases ResNet-34 $FAR$ at $FRR=5\%$ by what factor?
cards.back: Approximately 7 times (from $2.4\%$ to $16.1\%$).

cards.front: Why is Equal Error Rate (EER) an insufficient single metric for operational biometric security systems?
cards.back: Real systems operate at strict low-FAR thresholds rather than the artificial point where $FAR = FRR$.

cards.front: What metric evaluates speaker recognition false rejections when false alarms are constrained to 1 in 200 attempts?
cards.back: $FRR\text{@}FAR=0.5\%$

cards.front: In the NIST SRE Detection Cost Function ($minDCF$), what three parameters weight the detection errors?
cards.back: The cost of miss ($C_{miss}$), cost of false alarm ($C_{fa}$), and target prior probability ($P_{target}$).

cards.front: Why does standard Softmax cross-entropy loss underperform in open-set speaker recognition tasks?
cards.back: It optimizes linear class separability rather than intra-class compactness and angular margin on a hypersphere.

cards.front: How does Additive Angular Margin Softmax (AAM-Softmax / ArcFace) penalize feature vectors during training?
cards.back: By adding an angular margin penalty $m$ directly to the angle $\theta_y$ between normalized embeddings and class weights.

cards.front: In the AAM-Softmax loss equation $L = -\log \frac{e^{s \cos(\theta_{y} + m)}}{e^{s \cos(\theta_{y} + m)} + \sum_{j \neq y} e^{s \cos \theta_j}}$, what does $s$ represent?
cards.back: The feature scale parameter (hypersphere radius).

cards.front: What changes are made during the Large-Margin Fine-Tuning (LM-FT) stage compared to initial model pre-training?
cards.back: Audio segment duration increases (e.g., to 6 seconds), angular margin $m$ increases (e.g., to 0.5), and speed perturbation is disabled.

cards.front: What loss variation accommodates noisy internet speaker labels by maintaining multiple class centers?
cards.back: Sub-center ArcFace.

cards.front: What structural innovation allows SimAM (Simple Attention Module) to calculate 3D attention weights without extra parameters?
cards.back: An energy function derived from the spatial/channel distribution of individual neurons.

cards.front: Which ultra-large multilingual dataset containing over 110,000 speakers was used to train SimAM-ResNet34?
cards.back: VoxBlink2.

cards.front: Why does SimAM-ResNet34 out-perform deeper architectures like ResNet293 trained solely on VoxCeleb2?
cards.back: The massive scale and diversity of the VoxBlink2 training data outweigh architectural depth.

cards.front: What key architectural feature gives ERes2NetV2 superior performance across unseen domains?
cards.back: Local and global feature fusion (combining local acoustic changes with long-term vocal timbre).

cards.front: What is the EER of ERes2NetV2 on 2-second short speech segments from the VoxCeleb1-O test set?
What mechanism enables CAM++ to outperform ECAPA-TDNN while using only 7.2 million parameters?
cards.back: Context-Aware Masking on a D-TDNN backbone.

cards.front: Why was SpeechBrain's ECAPA-TDNN downgraded in the VoiceID model shortlist despite strong VoxCeleb performance?
cards.back: It suffered severe accuracy degradation when tested out-of-domain on CNCeleb ($8.01\%$ EER).

cards.front: What is Domain Mismatch in speaker recognition?
cards.back: The performance drop that occurs when testing a model on audio recorded in acoustic environments different from its training data.

cards.front: On the cross-domain CNCeleb benchmark, what happened to ResNet34's EER when moving from VoxCeleb data?
cards.back: EER degraded 9-fold from $0.723\%$ to $6.492\%$.

cards.front: How does simple unweighted Score Fusion of two distinct speaker models impact Open-Set False Alarm Rate?
cards.back: It reduces FAR by up to $44\%$ on large watchlists.

cards.front: What meta-features are utilized by Quality-aware Score Calibration (QMF) logistic regression?
cards.back: Cosine similarity, audio segment duration, embedding norms, and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

cards.front: By what percentage does QMF score calibration reduce False Alarm Rates across varying watchlist sizes?
cards.back: By approximately $21\%$ relative FAR reduction.

cards.front: Concept: Multi-Session Enrollment
cards.back: Definition: Averaging normalized speaker embeddings across multiple distinct recording sessions to reduce temporary channel and emotional noise.

cards.front: Why can Adaptive Score Normalization (AS-Norm) degrade performance in Open-Set Identification tasks?
cards.back: The maximum operator across a large watchlist can select cohort impostors that artificially distort top comparison scores.

cards.front: What voice activity detector (VAD) model is integrated into the VoiceID pre-processing pipeline?
cards.back: Silero VAD.

cards.front: What frequency cut-off is simulated when applying a Telephony Filter via resample transform?
cards.back: 4000 Hz (by downsampling 16 kHz audio to 8 kHz and upsampling back to 16 kHz).

cards.front: Why is tar-sharding (UIO / WebDataset format) required when processing millions of short audio files?
cards.back: It prevents Linux file system I/O bottlenecks and inode exhaustion by streaming large contiguous archive blocks.

cards.front: Which approximate nearest neighbor graph algorithm is used in FAISS for fast embedding retrieval?
cards.back: Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW).

cards.front: What condition must be met to keep an edge between nodes $u$ and $v$ under Mutual $k\text{-NN}$ filtering?
cards.back: Node $u$ must be in the top-$k$ neighbors of $v$, AND node $v$ must be in the top-$k$ neighbors of $u$.

cards.front: In the VoiceID clustering pipeline, what graph community detection algorithm is applied after Mutual $k\text{-NN}$ filtering?
cards.back: Leiden algorithm.

cards.front: What clustering method is used within oversized Leiden communities to prevent cluster over-merging?
cards.back: Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering (AHC) with average linkage.

cards.front: How are positive (same-speaker) trial pairs generated for threshold calibration without manual labels?
cards.back: By pairing non-adjacent split-half segments (e.g., 1st and 3rd quarters) extracted from the same long audio recording.

cards.front: How are negative (different-speaker) trial pairs generated for unlabeled threshold calibration?
cards.back: By sampling random pairs of audio files across a large corpus.

cards.front: What metric measures whether two halves of an unlabeled audio file are consistently assigned to the same cluster?
cards.back: Split-Half Consistency.

cards.front: What target value must Split-Half Consistency exceed to confirm proper cluster granularity?
What iterative steps constitute Pseudo-Label Training in semi-supervised speaker representation learning?
cards.back: Graph clustering $\rightarrow$ pseudo-label generation $\rightarrow$ AAM-Softmax fine-tuning $\rightarrow$ embedding extraction $\rightarrow$ re-clustering.

cards.front: What EER level can self-supervised ArcFace fine-tuning achieve on VoxCeleb without human-annotated speaker labels?
cards.back: Approximately $0.99\% \text{--} 1.01\%$ EER.

cards.front: What is the primary target dataset container and audio codec used in Telegram voice messages?
cards.back: Ogg container with Opus audio codec.

cards.front: What acoustic evaluation protocol uses the VoxCeleb1 dataset split into gender- and nationality-matched pairs?
cards.back: Vox1-H (Hard) protocol.

cards.front: What cross-domain speaker recognition benchmark features 3,000 speakers across 11 different genres?
cards.back: CNCeleb.

cards.front: What public corpus containing volunteer voice recordings and $client\_id$ metadata provides ready-to-use speaker labels for benchmark split creation?
cards.back: Mozilla Common Voice.

cards.front: Discriminative Fine-Tuning applies a learning rate of $3 \times 10^{-6}$ to the Wav2Vec2 frontend and _____ to the classification head.
Concept: Double Dipping in machine learning evaluation
cards.back: Definition: Reusing the validation set for early stopping, hyperparameter tuning, and reporting final test accuracy.

cards.front: Why is returning zero-tensors on audio read failures dangerous during neural network dataset iteration?
cards.back: It silently trains the neural network on silent audio frames labeled as valid data, corrupting gradients.

cards.front: What is the primary architectural component of the WaveFakeModel used for deepfake detection?
cards.back: A pre-trained Wav2Vec2 SSL frontend followed by mean temporal pooling and a linear classifier.

cards.front: What metric balances Detection Error Tradeoff by plotting false rejection rate against false alarm rate on logarithmic axes?
cards.back: Detection Error Tradeoff (DET) curve.

cards.front: In A-Softmax (SphereFace), what type of angular margin multiplier $m$ is applied to the target angle?
cards.back: Multiplicative angular margin.

cards.front: In CosFace (AM-Softmax), how is the margin $m$ applied to the target logit?
cards.back: As an additive cosine margin subtracted from $\cos \theta_y$.

cards.front: What audio feature extractor combines 1D time-domain convolutions with Sinc-based band-pass filters?
cards.back: SincNet.

cards.front: What is the minimum recommended speech duration for extracting stable deep speaker embeddings in production?
cards.back: 3.0 seconds of active speech.

cards.front: Why are raw pre-trained WavLM base embeddings insufficient as direct speaker verification embeddings without fine-tuning?
cards.back: They retain high phonetic and semantic information rather than speaker-exclusive timbre characteristics.

cards.front: What speaker recognition baseline achieves a $0.52\%$ EER on VoxCeleb1-O by combining a WavLM front-end with an AAM-TDNN back-end?
cards.back: WavLM-TDNN with joint fine-tuning.

cards.front: In speaker embedding extraction, what pooling layer aggregates temporal frame features into segment-level representations using attention weights?
cards.back: Attentive Statistics Pooling (ASP).

cards.front: What is the standard sampling rate required by most pre-trained deep speaker recognition models?
cards.back: 16 kHz (16,000 samples per second).

cards.front: What mathematical metric is standard for computing distance between two normalized $L_2$ speaker embedding vectors?
cards.back: Cosine similarity (or Euclidean distance on unit sphere).

cards.front: Which Python library is standard for loading audio, computing MFCCs, and generating Mel-spectrograms in research pipelines?
cards.back: Librosa.

cards.front: In speaker diarization, what two steps follow audio segmentation?
cards.back: Embedding extraction for each segment and intra-recording clustering.

cards.front: Why is speed perturbation disabled during Large-Margin Fine-Tuning of speaker encoders?
cards.back: Speed perturbation alters vocal tract pitch scale, which can blur subtle timbral differences when fine-tuning margins.

cards.front: What happens to false alarm rate ($FAR$) in an Open-Set System as watchlist size approaches infinity without score normalization?
cards.back: $FAR_{OSI}$ approaches $100\%$.

cards.front: What open-source deep learning framework developed by Horizon Robotics provides end-to-end speaker verification recipes and C++/Python runtimes?
cards.back: WeSpeaker.

cards.front: In Python string formatting, why does applying the `:.2%` specifier to a rate variable already multiplied by 100 cause an error?
cards.back: The `:.2%` specifier automatically multiplies the number by 100 a second time.

cards.front: What heuristic limits candidate search space when clustering audio messages within individual 1:1 chat channels?
cards.back: A 1:1 chat context inherently limits the maximum number of unique speakers to 2.

cards.front: What role does SpecAugment play during speaker encoder GPU training?
cards.back: It provides online data augmentation by masking random blocks of frequency channels and time steps.

cards.front: What happens to the EER gap between weak and strong speaker architectures when evaluation speech duration drops from full length to 2 seconds?
cards.back: The performance gap between weak and strong architectures doubles.

cards.front: What is the parameter count of the CAM++ speaker embedding model?
cards.back: 7.2 million parameters.

cards.front: In biometric verification, what error occurs when a valid enrolled target speaker is rejected by the system?
cards.back: False Rejection (Type II Error / Miss).

cards.front: In biometric verification, what error occurs when an un-enrolled impostor is accepted as a watchlist target?
cards.back: False Alarm (Type I Error / False Accept).
